content.text: medically managed pts: osteoporosis = treated w bisphos; for marked hypercalcemia: calcitonin (salmon) 4 to 8 IU/kg SC every 12 h; can ↓Ca by 1 to 2 mg/dL w.in a few hrs.

Tx of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women and in men: 10 mg daily or 70 mg (tablet or PO solution) Q1wk. Swallow tablets whole w/ 6-8 oz plain H2O at least 30 min b4 the first food, drink, or med of the day. ⍉ lie down for at least 30 min after taking and until after food.

CI: abnormalities of the esophagus which delay esophageal emptying such as stricture or achalasia. CI: inability to stand or sit upright for at least 30 min. CI: hypocalcemia. Esophageal rxns (esophagitis, ulcers, erosions) reported; be alert for signs and instruct pts to d/c and seek medical attention for dysphagia, odynophagia, retrosternal pain, or new/worsening heartburn. Hypocalcemia must be corrected b4 initiating therapy. Severe bone, joint, musc pain may occur; d/c use if severe Sx develop. ONJ reported (can occur spontaneously; generally assoc w/ tooth extraction and/or local infect w/ delayed heal). Atypical frx incl femoral frx reported; pts w/ new thigh or groin pain should be evaluated to r/o a femoral frx; re-evaluate risk/benefit and consider interrupting bisphos therapy. ⍉recommended if CrCl < 35 mL/min. Calcium, antacids, or PO meds containing multivalent cations interfere w/ absorb; instruct pts to wait at least one-half hr after FOSAMAX b4 any other PO med. OD: hypocalcemia, hypophosphatemia, and upper GI adverse events may result; give milk or antacids to bind alendronate; ⍉ induce vomiting (risk of esophageal irritate); keep the pt fully upright.

CI: hypersensitivity to calcitonin salmon or any of the excipients (rxns incl anaphylaxis w/ death, bronchospasm, and swelling of the tongue or throat). Serious hypersensitivity rxns incl fatal anaphylaxis reported; consider skin testing b4 tx in pts w/ sus hypersensitivity to calcitonin salmon. Hypocalcemia w/ tetany (musc cramps, twitching) and sz activity reported; hypocalcemia must be corrected b4 initiating therapy. Meta-analysis of 21 trials suggests an ↑ risk of overall malig in calcitonin salmon-treated pts. Circulating antibodies to calcitonin salmon may develop and may cause loss of response to tx. Use for Paget's dz or postmenopausal osteoporosis = recommended w/ an adequate intake of Ca and vitD. Concomitant lithium may ↓ plasma lithium concentrations (↑ urinary clearance); lithium dose may require adj. OD: hypocalcemic tetany could occur; keep parenteral calcium available for tx. MC adverse rxns: nausea w/ or w/o vomiting (10%), inj site inflam (10%), and flushing of the face or hands (2% to 5%). ←the poss assoc b/n malig and calcitonin salmon use, the need for continued therapy should be re-evaluated periodically.
